previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a previous stroke was admitted for evaluation of substernal chest pain radiating to the left shoulder, occurring during physical activity and emotional stress. Initial concerns for acute coronary syndrome were ruled out by normal cardiac enzymes, unchanged EKG, and no acute findings on chest X-ray. The pain was reproducible on chest wall palpation, leading to a diagnosis of costochondritis. Her blood pressure was elevated on admission, likely due to medication noncompliance, and improved with reinitiation of home antihypertensives. She remained on her baseline medications for diabetes, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and depression. She was discharged home with instructions to use acetaminophen for pain, continue all chronic medications, and follow up with her primary care provider and cardiologist.

Acute Issues:

# Gastroenteritis: Pt with a 1 day history of N/V/D which has 
since resolved in less than 24 hours. Patient has presented in 
last month with similar symptoms with negative CT abd/pelvis. 
Symptoms have been present for <24 hours and are most likely 
viral in nature as she has no white count and no fever. On last 
presentation, however, she had an elevated lactate. We checked 
lactate and it was normal so no evidence of end organ ischemia. 
Pt has a significant cardiac history which puts her at risk for 
mesenteric ischemia, however, with normal CT on last similar 
presentation, this seems less likely. With supportive care with 
hydration, encourage PO pt symtpoms improved.

# Chest pain: Patient has had multiple admissions with 
complaints of substernal chest pain. Ruled out on prior 
admissions and recent stress without evidence of reversible 
ischemia. EKG with <1mm ST changes and nonspecific TWI. Two sets 
of troponins were negative. No evidence on CXR of lung process 
that may be contributing. GI upset from nausea may be causing 
the pain as patient has GERD.  
Pt ruled out for ACS we did not pursue further cardiac work-up 
as chest pain appears to be related to GI causes as patient has 
been vomiting. We continued her on home cardiac meds including 
isosorbide dinitrate, aspirin 325mg, plavix.  We also continued 
her ranitidine and aluminum-mag-simethicone for GERD. 
 
# Acute kidney injury: Creatinine was elevated to 1.4 from 
baseline 1.1-1.2. Patient has had several similar bumps in the 
setting of diarrhea/vomiting in the past. Likely prerenal 
etiology. She received 1L NS in ED and is taking po's without 
issue now. She was given addition fluid boluses and her kidney 
function improved to baseline

# HTN/HL: BP not well controlled at this time with SBP in 150's. 
 We continued her on home amlodipine, lisinopril, 
chlorthalidone, metoprolol succinate. We continued home 
atorvastatin as well. Pt will need titration of BP meds for 
better control  

# DMII: Blood glucose elevated on this admission to 390. We 
continued home lantus BID with humalog SS but held metformin 
secondary to elevated creatinine. Pt was discharged on home meds 
of lantus, humalog ISS, and metformin.  
 
# Asthma: lungs clear without evidence of exacerbation. 
Continued albuterol and fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 BID.
